indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2.5.1.1: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Explain how to keep the body clean and describe why it is important

skills.description: Describe ways to keep the body clean
Explain why keeping the body clean is important
Explain why we trim our finger nails and hair
Explain why we should not share personal items
Demonstrate or describe how to use items for trimming hair and nails correctly

misconceptions: You only need to keep your body clean when you are visibly dirty.
Trimming nails and hair is only for looking good, not for health.
Sharing combs and towels is fine because they are just for grooming.
Bathing once a week is enough.
Germs only live in dirt you can see.
Wearing clean clothes is not part of personal hygiene.

questions.stem: Which of these is a good way to keep your body clean?
questions.explanation: Bathing with soap and water is one of the best ways to keep your body clean.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think playing in the mud is a way to clean.

questions.stem: What should you use to clean your teeth?
hints: You use it in your mouth.
questions.explanation: A toothbrush and toothpaste are used to clean your teeth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse items used for different hygiene routines.

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep your body clean?
questions.explanation: Keeping your body clean prevents germs from making you sick.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the link between hygiene and health.

questions.stem: How often should you take a bath?
questions.explanation: You should bathe every day to remove dirt and germs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think bathing once a week is enough.

questions.stem: Should you share your toothbrush with a friend?
options: Yes, if they are your best friend
questions.explanation: You should not share your toothbrush because it can spread germs from one person to another.
questions.misconception: Pupils may share personal items with friends without knowing the risks.

questions.stem: Why should you cut your finger nails regularly?
options: To keep them clean and prevent dirt from hiding under them
To make them sharp like a knife
hints: Dirt gets stuck under long nails.
questions.explanation: Cutting your nails keeps them short and clean, preventing dirt and germs from hiding underneath.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think long nails are just a style choice.

questions.stem: Why do we wear clean clothes?
options: To stay clean and avoid skin diseases
questions.explanation: Wearing clean clothes helps keep your skin clean and prevents skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think clothes only need washing when visibly dirty.

questions.stem: Ama and her sister use the same comb. Why is this a bad idea?
options: They can spread germs like lice or ringworm
hints: What is on the comb after use?
questions.explanation: Sharing a comb can spread germs, lice, or skin diseases like ringworm from one person to another.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sharing is always good without considering germs.

questions.stem: Which of these is part of keeping your body clean?
questions.explanation: Washing your hands before eating is an important part of personal hygiene.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see hand-washing as part of body cleanliness.

questions.stem: What can happen if you do not keep your body clean?
options: You can get skin diseases and fall sick
questions.explanation: Not keeping your body clean allows germs to grow, which can cause skin diseases and other sicknesses.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect poor hygiene to illness.

questions.stem: What should you use to cut your finger nails?
questions.explanation: A nail cutter or nail clipper is the correct tool for trimming finger nails.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say teeth or a knife, which are dangerous.

questions.stem: Name two things you need to bathe.
questions.explanation: You need water and soap (and a sponge and towel) to bathe.

questions.stem: Why is it dangerous to bite your finger nails?
options: It can damage your teeth and allow germs into your body
It makes your nails grow faster
It is good for your health
hints: Teeth are not for biting nails.
questions.explanation: Biting your nails can damage your teeth and allow germs from under the nails to enter your body, making you sick.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think biting nails is harmless.

questions.stem: Why should you not share a towel with someone who has a skin disease?
options: The towel might be too small
The germs from their skin can transfer to you
questions.explanation: Sharing a towel with an infected person can transfer germs to your skin, causing you to catch the disease.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize diseases can spread through shared items.

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep your finger nails clean?
options: Because you use your fingers to eat and touch your face, and germs can enter your body
hints: What do you do with your fingers?
How do germs get into your body?
questions.explanation: You use your fingers for many tasks, including eating. If your nails are dirty, germs can enter your body and make you sick.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think nail hygiene is only about appearance.

questions.stem: Show your teacher how to correctly use a nail cutter to trim your nails.
hints: Do not cut too close to the skin.
questions.explanation: This tests the safe and correct use of a nail cutter.

questions.stem: Describe how you keep your body clean each day. Write at least three things you do.

criteria.description: Mentions washing hands or wearing clean clothes

hints: What do you do in the bathroom?
questions.explanation: A daily routine includes bathing, brushing teeth, and washing hands.

questions.stem: Explain why keeping your body clean is important for your health.

criteria.description: States that it prevents germs from entering the body
States that it prevents sickness or skin diseases

hints: What do germs do to your body?
questions.explanation: Keeping clean removes germs and prevents sickness.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher two personal items you should not share and explain why.

criteria.description: Names a personal item (e.g., toothbrush, towel, comb)
Explains that sharing can spread germs or diseases

hints: What do you use on your body only?
Why is it bad to share?
questions.explanation: Items like toothbrushes, towels, and combs should not be shared because they can spread germs.
